Japanese LLMs in 2026: PLaMo 3.0 Prime and Sakana Namazu

Preferred Networks shipped PLaMo 3.0 Prime in June 2026 with a 256K context window. Sakana AI followed with Sakana Namazu, an OpenAI-compatible API tuned on Japanese business text on top of Kimi K2.6. Neither is a drop-in DeepL replacement, but both claim more natural EN-JA than gpt-4o-mini.

APIs you can actually call from a Worker

PLaMo Prime speaks chat completions at api.platform.preferredai.jp. Sakana Namazu uses api.sakana.ai/v1. The consumer web apps (translate.preferredai.jp and Sakana Translate) do not expose the same contract.

  • plamo-3.0-prime: set reasoning_effort to none, raise max_tokens.
  • sakana-namazu: turn thinking off; do not enable web_search for clipping.
  • DeepL API Growth is a monthly floor around the same size as Workers Paid. Fine for CAT tools, noisy for a personal queue.

A request shape that survived 2026-09-20

{
  "model": "plamo-3.0-prime",
  "reasoning_effort": "none",
  "max_tokens": 16000,
  "response_format": { "type": "json_schema" }
}

Hugging Face still hosts pfnet/plamo-2-translate for self-hosting. That model is the specialized translator, but it is not what the public PLaMo API serves. A Cloudflare Worker should not grow a GPU sidecar to prove a point about knowledge cutoff.

If a 2026 product name is translated into a paraphrase, the model is guessing. Keep PLaMo 3.0 Prime, Sakana Namazu, DeepL, and gpt-4.1-mini in the original Latin spelling on first mention, then write Japanese around them.
